title: Session Clipboards — scratchpad for portable conversation bookmarks
content:
Context and problem 

Quick note: this is a personal scratchpad for an idea I sketched after a customer call (fintech startup) where they asked for simple, low-friction ways for end-users to save and reapply parts of a conversation. The ask: non-technical users want to 'clip' a helpful assistant reply (or a set of turns) and re-use that as an input later, across devices and assistant instances, without needing to create a formal template or prompt library.

High-level idea (one-liner)

Session Clipboards: a lightweight, shareable bookmark for a window of conversation (1–n turns) that preserves necessary context, key metadata (source, timestamp, fidelity tier), and an optional transformation (condense / anonymize / convert to instruction) so the clipboard can be pasted into future sessions or shared with teammates.

Why this matters
- Low friction for end-users increases retention and perceived utility.
- Enables reuse of high-quality agent outputs without exposing entire session history.
- Helps customers standardize recurring tasks (e.g., cover-letter generator, compliance-safe reply templates) without building a full prompt management UI.

Primary personas
- Product user (non-technical): wants to save a good answer to re-run later.
- Power user (team lead): collects curated clipboards to share across teammates.
- Platform admin: wants auditability and ability to limit clipboards to certain models/tiers.

Proposed core flows (MVP scope)
1) Create clip: user highlights one or more assistant replies (or selects last N turns) -> click "Clip" -> choose options: title (auto-suggest), privacy (private/shared/org), fidelity (exact / condensed), redact-sensitive (on/off). Backend: snapshot of selected text + lightweight context tokens (e.g., instruction + last user prompt) + metadata.

2) Paste clip: in any new session, user opens clip picker -> choose clipboard -> decide insert mode: inject as system instruction / as user message / as pinned context (read-only). Runtime merges clipboard content into session with a clear provenance banner.

3) Share & discover: clip can be shared via link or added to a team collection. Team clips are discoverable in a small catalog (search by tags).

User stories
- As a customer support agent, I want to clip a canonical troubleshooting reply so I can paste it into future tickets and tweak it per case.
- As a hiring manager, I want to save a well-phrased interview feedback summary and reuse it across candidates.
- As a compliance officer, I want to mark a clip as "sensitive" so it cannot be exported outside the org.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Clip creation: UI control to clip selected turns, saved to user's personal clip store within 2s.
- Clip paste: Clips are insertable in a new session with three insert modes. Insertion preserves the label and a short provenance banner.
- Privacy controls: default private, option to share to org; org clips require admin approval to publish.
- Storage: Clips store only the minimal context required (do not store raw user PII by default). Optionally run a redaction step before saving.
- Telemetry: emit events for create / paste / share with clip id + user + model_variant.

Metrics to watch
- Clip creation rate (clips per active user / week).
- Paste-to-create ratio (how often created clips are reused). Target >= 0.4 for early validation.
- Time-to-paste (how quickly users find/paste clips after creation).
- Clip share rate and team adoption (org-level clips / org active users).

Architecture notes (runtime & storage)
- Clip representation: small JSON record with fields: title, excerpt, full_text (optional), minimal_context (instruction + last_user_prompt), tags, owner_id, visibility, created_at, redaction_status, model_hints (preferred model / fidelity).
- Storage: primary store in user-scoped DB (encrypted at rest). For org-shared clips, replicate index in org catalog.
- Runtime insertion: treat clip as either a system message or user message at session bootstrap. Use our safe-insertion path to avoid token duplication (dedupe prefixes).
- Redaction step: pipeline option to call a PII classifier before save, store redacted_text + redaction_log. (For MVP, make redaction opt-in to avoid blocking).

UX wireframe (text)
- Inline clip button on each assistant reply: small scissor/clip icon -> modal: title (auto), scope toggle (private/team), fidelity dropdown (exact/condense), tags. Save.
- In composer: small "Clip" icon opens modal/side sheet with search, filters, create quick clip, import from URL.

Risks and tradeoffs
- Privacy: storing snippets may capture PII; we need a conservative default and opt-in for cloud storage for some customers.
- Explosion of low-quality clips: need lightweight moderation (user flags) and team curation workflows.
- Complexity vs. value: don't want to build full prompt library; aim to be a small, discoverable layer.

Alternatives considered
- Full prompt library (too heavy for MVP).
- Automatic auto-saves of every assistant reply -> noise and storage costs.
- Browser/bookmarklet approach (client-only) -> good privacy but poor cross-device/team shareability.

Implementation plan (3 sprints)
Sprint 1 (discovery + prototype): define clip format, basic UI for clip creation and paste in web composer, backend store, telemetry. (2 weeks)
Sprint 2 (improvements): search, tags, team sharing, basic redaction toggle, admin visibility controls. (3 weeks)
Sprint 3 (polish + scale): UI polish, org catalog, audit logs, storage retention policy, mobile composer insertion. (3–4 weeks)

Open questions / action items
- MVP redaction policy: default redact PII or only flag? (Ask security/compliance).
- Retention and export policy for clips (ops/legal input).
- Should clip insertion be token-count-aware and offer automatic condensation to respect session budgets? (Eng feasibility + Optimize team?).
- UX: where to surface clips in low-friction flows (composer top bar vs. message actions).

Notes to self / quick todo
- Talk to Erin (Legal) about export controls for org clips.
- Quick prototype in web composer dev branch; ask Maya for a quick UX sketch.
- Add a simple rule: if saved clip length > 1k chars, auto-suggest "condense" before save.


End of scratchpad.

(Branch idea: "Clipboard bundles" = group multiple clips into a single publishable 'playbook' — maybe later.)
